injuries.name: Dalton Schultz
injuries.shortComment: Schultz caught four of six targets for 33 yards in Sunday's 34-31 win over the Jaguars.
injuries.longComment: Schultz actually led the team with his six targets, but C.J. Stroud spread the ball around to 10 different pass catchers on a day he attempted 34 passes. Schultz has been held to 35 yards or fewer in five of six games this season and has yet to visit the end zone. He's a low-floor, low-ceiling fantasy bet ahead of next Sunday's date with the Giants.

injuries.name: Jawhar Jordan
injuries.shortComment: Jordan rushed six times for 43 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 34-31 win over the Jaguars. He added one catch for seven yards on one target.
injuries.longComment: With David Montgomery (groin) out, Jordan was called up from the practice squad for Sunday's game and logged 14 offensive snaps behind Woody Marks' 49 out of the backfield. Jordan's big play was a 25-yard touchdown scamper in the third quarter that gave Houston a 31-21 lead. Montgomery is considered week-to-week, so Jordan could again play a significant role behind Marks next Sunday against the Giants.

injuries.name: Foster Moreau
injuries.shortComment: Moreau caught both of his targets for seven yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 34-31 win over the Jaguars in London.
injuries.longComment: Moreau made the most of his two opportunities, securing a pair of red-zone scores from one and six yards. Three of Moreau's 11 grabs this season have resulted in red-zone touchdowns. He can mostly be ignored in fantasy football while Dalton Schultz is healthy.

injuries.name: Jaylin Noel
injuries.shortComment: Noel gathered in all four targets for 107 yards and one touchdown during Sunday's 34-31 win against the Jaguars in London.
injuries.longComment: Noel has made much of his mark on special teams through five games this season, including two kick returns for 65 yards and one punt return for two yards in Week 6. However, he reached the end zone for a second consecutive game on a 13-yard connection with QB C.J. Stroud, and Noel's receiving-yardage total easily bested his previous career high of 85 yards, which he managed in Week 4 against the Cowboys. Nico Collins remains the top dog in the Texans' receiving corps, and Marvin Harrison just showed up from Arizona via trade, but Noel appears to have built a nice rapport with Stroud as his second season has gone on.

injuries.name: Woody Marks
injuries.shortComment: Marks carried the ball 15 times for 56 yards and caught two of three targets for 25 yards in Sunday's 34-31 win over the Jaguars.
injuries.longComment: With David Montgomery (groin) inactive, Marks led the Texans backfield in touches and scrimmage yards, but practice-squad elevation Jawhar Jordan arguably made a bigger splash with 43 rushing yards and a touchdown on just six carries. Jordan showed some upside late last season when pressed into duty as well, so even if Montgomery's absence continues, Marks could see his workload shrink. Marks will take on the Giants in Week 7.

injuries.name: Marvin Harrison Jr.
injuries.shortComment: Harrison caught three of four targets for 34 yards in Sunday's 34-31 win over the Jaguars.
injuries.longComment: Making his Texans debut, Harrison wasn't especially productive on his own, but quarterback C.J. Stroud seemed to benefit from his presence and spread the ball around to 10 different pass catchers. The three grabs still tied Harrison's season high, giving him something to build on as he looks to put his disappointing Cardinals tenure behind him. The two former Ohio State teammates will look to re-buiild their chemistry further in Week 7 against the Giants.

injuries.name: C.J. Stroud
injuries.shortComment: Stroud completed 24 of 34 passes for 312 yards and three touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 34-31 win over the Jaguars. He added five yards on his only carry.
injuries.longComment: With Marvin Harrison making his Texans debut, Stroud spread the ball around to 10 different pass catchers as he set a new season high in TD passes and topped 300 yards for the third time in six games. The QB did throw his first INT of the season at a potentially crucial time, getting picked off by Travis Hunter in the end zone in the fourth quarter, but Stroud made up for it by putting together a game-winning field goal drive as time expired on his next possession. He'll take a 9:1 TD:INT into a Week 7 clash with the Giants.

injuries.name: Nico Collins
injuries.shortComment: Collins caught three of five targets for 74 yards in Sunday's 34-31 win over the Jaguars. He added five yards on his only carry.
injuries.longComment: C.J. Stroud spread the ball around to 10 different pass catchers, and Jaylin Noel wound up being the most productive of the bunch with a 4-107-1 line. Collins still hit for a 42-yard gain on his first catch of the day, helping to set up a Foster Moreau TD in the first quarter. Collins has topped 70 receiving yards in three of his four games this season, compiling a 22-323-3 line on 30 targets. He'll take on an injury-thinned Giants secondary at home in Week 7.

injuries.name: Reed Blankenship
injuries.shortComment: Blankenship (concussion) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Jaguars in London.
injuries.longComment: Blankenship was deemed to have a concussion by one of the NFL's independent neurologists. The safety has now entered the league's five-step concussion protocol and will not participate in full-contact practices or games until he is cleared. M.J. Stewart will likely finish the game at strong safety alongside Calen Bullock.

injuries.name: Azeez Al-Shaair
injuries.shortComment: Al-Shaair has cleared concussion protocol and will be available for the second half of Sunday's game against the Jaguars, Jonathan M. Alexander of the Houston Chronicle reports.
injuries.longComment: Al-Shaair was being evaluated by medical staff for a possible concussion in the second quarter. The veteran linebacker has passed all the benchmarks and will be back on the field for the second half of Sunday's contest in London.

injuries.name: Ja'Marcus Ingram
injuries.shortComment: Ingram (elbow) is active for Sunday's game against the Jaguars in London.
injuries.longComment: Listed as questionable heading into Sunday, Ingram had been expected to suit up against Jacksonville after he closed Week 6 prep with a pair of full practices before being officially reinstated from injured reserve Saturday. The 29-year-old will likely handle a depth role in the Houston secondary and will be featured on the special-teams units.

injuries.name: Henry To'oTo'o
injuries.shortComment: To'oTo'o (shoulder) is active for Sunday's game against the Jaguars in London.
injuries.longComment: The 25-year-old linebacker had been listed as questionable heading into Sunday's contest, but after being activated from injured reserve Saturday, the writing was on the wall for him to suit up in London. To'oTo'o will be suiting up for the first time since the Texans' Week 1 loss to the Bills, when he exited in the fourth quarter after injuring his shoulder.

injuries.name: Tank Dell
injuries.shortComment: The Texans ruled out Dell (knee) for Sunday's game against the Jaguars in London.
injuries.longComment: Currently in the midst of his second week of practicing with the Texans after having his 21-day evaluation window opened Oct. 7, Dell has taken a notable step forward in his recovery from a severe left knee injury by turning in back-to-back full sessions Wednesday and Thursday. Though the Texans won't bring him back from injured reserve for the London game, Dell stands a strong chance of being activated ahead of the team's Oct. 25 matchup with the Giants and seeing his first game action since December 2024 if he can continue to practice without restrictions next week.

injuries.name: Kayshon Boutte
injuries.shortComment: Boutte caught three of five targets for 38 yards during Sunday's 26-3 win over the Titans.
injuries.longComment: Boutte finished tied with fellow wide receivers Xavier Hutchinson and Jaylin Noel for second on the team in targets, and his 38 receiving yards set a new season high for him. With Houston acquiring Marvin Harrison from the Cardinals on Sunday, it's unclear how the wide receiver room will be organized moving forward. On the season, Boutte has caught 12 of 18 targets for 153 yards over five contests.
